scale.na: N/A needs a reason, like a score does. N/A outside na_allowed fails schema validation.

na_conditions.first_unit: The unit is the first unit of the draft.
na_conditions.reveals_nothing: The unit reveals no answer, result or conclusion.

criteria.name: Highly visual
criteria.question: Does a chart, infographic, cartoon or shape carry the idea, and does the slide look different from the one before it?

anchors.1: Text only, or the only image is a logo or a small icon. The slide looks the same as the one before it.
anchors.3: A visual is present but decorates the words rather than carrying the idea, or the slide repeats the previous slide's look.
anchors.5: A chart, infographic, cartoon or shape carries the idea, and the slide looks different from the one before it. A logo or a small icon does not count.

criteria.name: Clear wording
criteria.question: Does the wording stand alone in full sentences and plain words?

anchors.1: Fragments, trendy compressions or coined jargon. A reader cannot follow it without the speaker or the author.
anchors.3: Mostly full sentences in plain words, with one fragment, one compression or one undefined term.
anchors.5: Stands alone. Full sentences, plain words, no fragments, no trendy compressions, no coined jargon.

criteria.name: Flow
criteria.question: Is the logic step from the previous unit to this one obvious without the speaker?

anchors.1: No visible link to the previous unit. The step needs the speaker, or the unit is out of order.
anchors.3: The link exists but the reader has to work it out, or it depends on a line only the speaker says.
anchors.5: A logic step from the previous unit to this one is obvious without the speaker.

criteria.name: Surprise and delight
criteria.question: Is this unit part of a journey that involves, teases or tricks the audience, without giving away an answer before its moment?

anchors.1: A preview that gives away an answer before its moment, or a flat statement with nothing for the audience to do or feel. A recurring character appears as decoration.
anchors.3: Some tension or involvement, but the payoff is predictable, or a small spoiler lands early.
anchors.5: A journey, not a preview. A map of the session's shape is fine; giving away an answer before its moment is not, except a tagged hook paid off later. The audience is involved, teased or tricked. A recurring character returns as a callback where it helps, never as decoration.

criteria.name: One idea per unit
criteria.question: Does the unit carry exactly one idea?

anchors.1: Three or more ideas compete, or there is no idea at all.
anchors.3: One main idea with a second idea that pulls attention away from it.
anchors.5: One idea per slide, or per section part.

criteria.name: Concrete before abstract
criteria.question: Does an example or case come before the principle?

anchors.1: The principle comes alone, with no example or case anywhere.
anchors.3: An example is present but comes after the principle, or is too general to picture.
anchors.5: An example or case comes before the principle.

criteria.name: Guess before reveal
criteria.question: Judged on this slide with the one before it, does the audience get to predict before the answer lands?

anchors.1: The answer lands with no chance to predict it.
anchors.3: A prediction is possible but not invited, or the previous slide half gives the answer away.
anchors.5: The audience predicts before the answer lands, judged on this slide with the one before.

criteria.name: Earns its place
criteria.question: Would cutting this unit lose something?

anchors.1: A unit that repeats a neighbour. Cutting it loses nothing.
anchors.3: It adds something, but a neighbour could absorb it with one sentence.
anchors.5: Cutting it would lose something the draft needs.

criteria.name: Honest numbers
criteria.question: Does every number carry its source and its limit?

anchors.1: A number with no source and no limit.
anchors.3: Every number has a source, but a limit is missing, or the source is vague.
anchors.5: Every number has its source and its limit, on the slide, in the notes, or in the article's references.

arc.inputs: Every unit's text and notes in order, the run sheet, and a contact sheet of all screenshots. One call per round per grader.

criteria.name: Flow
criteria.question: Does each unit follow from the one before, across the whole draft?

criteria.name: Surprise and delight
criteria.question: Is the whole draft a journey that involves, teases or tricks the audience?

criteria.name: Participation
criteria.question: Is the audience involved often enough, judged against the run sheet's own act windows and exercise timings?

anchors.1: Long stretches with nothing for the audience to do, against the run sheet's own windows.
anchors.3: Involvement exists but clusters, leaving at least one act window passive.
anchors.5: Every act window involves the audience, at the timings the run sheet sets.

arc.hook_payoff: Every [hook:<name>] tag in the notes has a matching [payoff:<name>] tag later.

bars.split_regrade: Where one grader gives 3 and the other 4 or more, the lower grader re-grades that unit once and the second score stands.
